# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

• **Start with your revenue reality, not your wishlist.** Audit what your coaches actually deliver right now (group classes, 1:1 PT, nutrition plans, challenges, etc.). Price based on what you're *consistently* selling, not what sounds good. This prevents menu bloat and coach confusion.

• **Create TWO documents, not one.** Coaches need a pricing/commission structure (what they earn per service, upsell triggers). Members need a clean visual menu showing class types, PT packages, and add-ons. Different audiences = different info density.

• **Build a simple decision tree for pricing tiers.** For PT specifically: e.g., "4-pack (drop-in rate) vs. 8-pack (10% discount) vs. unlimited monthly." This nudges members toward higher-value packages without overwhelming choice. Same logic for any membership add-ons.

• **Lock in ONE person as "menu owner" (probably you).** Give coaches 1 week to flag what's missing or broken, then finalize. Otherwise you'll be re-writing it every month. Make it live on your website, in-gym, and in your booking system simultaneously—no version confusion.

• **Test pricing on your most loyal members first.** Before rolling out publicly, get feedback from 3-5 regulars. They'll spot if something doesn't make sense or if pricing feels off. One conversation beats guessing.

What's your current pricing situation—are you charging at all for PT right now, or starting from scratch?

# The Forge — Fractional CFO Review

## REVENUE ANALYSIS: Growth stalling, member quality declining
**Trend:** Last 3 months (Jul–Sep) avg £19.3k vs prior 3 (Apr–Jun, ex-April relocation) = £16.2k (+19% uplift, solid). *But* Sep revenue +£5.9k from Aug is almost entirely member headcount (+16 to 169), not pricing power. **Rev/member collapsed from £145 (July) to £106 (Aug) to £130 (Sep)** — you're onboarding lower-paying tiers or losing premium upsell capture.

**Churn spike in May (12.8%) signals onboarding quality issue.** Since recovered, but membership is volatile — retention is your weak point, not acquisition.

### INCREASE REVENUE — actionable moves:
- **Audit your member tier mix NOW.** You have 169 members generating £22k/month = £130/head avg, but July was £145 at 136 members. You've added 33 members since July but only £0.2k incremental revenue. Either new sign-ups are on a cheaper tier, or you're not upselling existing members to premium/class packs. Segment by tier and identify the discount cohort — if they're trial-to-paid converts, that's fine; if they're underbidding established members, reprice them at next renewal.
- **Launch a 12-month pre-pay discount (save 10%, lock to £12–13/month effective).** Your monthly churn averages 6.2% = ~1 member lost per 16 paying; annual pre-pay halves that visibility risk and improves cash predictability. Model: if 20% of your 169 convert, that's +£25–30k cash upfront, 15% gross margin boost.
- **Plug the May churn lesson — tighten onboarding.** 12.8% churn suggests weak trial-to-paid conversion or poor induction. Introduce a Day-3 "goals & class schedule" check-in call (staff or automatable via Typeform) to catch at-risk members before cancellation. Target: reduce churn to 4% (industry benchmark for fitness is 5–6%).
- **Introduce a class pack upsell at sign-up and at month 3.** If members are at £130/head, 80% are likely on unlimited. Launch a "10-class pass" at £99 (£9.90/class) as an entry point, then upsell 30%
